name: Wuhan Tianhe International Airport
before:
Central China's busiest airport, and the one that sits nearest the middle of the country's route network, which is why so many internal connections route through it. It handled just over 31.3 million passengers in 2025, making it the fourteenth busiest in China.

It is a hub for both China Eastern and China Southern, with Air China treating it as a focus city, so domestic coverage from here is unusually good for a city this far from the coast.

The detail that matters most for booking is the transit visa. Since 2019, passengers from 53 countries, including EU states, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the United States, can enter China through this airport without a Chinese visa for up to 144 hours when they are transiting onward to a third country. That opens up a genuine stopover, though the onward third country condition is strict.

The airport opened in 1995 and lies 26 km north of the city in Huangpi District. The name Tianhe means Sky River, an old Chinese name for the Milky Way.
after:
Central China's busiest airport, 26 km north of Wuhan in Huangpi District. It handled just over 31.3 million passengers in 2025, making it the 14th busiest in China.

For UK clients the rule that matters is entry: British passport holders can enter China without a visa for up to 30 days, including in transit, until 31 December 2026. Check the position for any trip after that date.

The airport opened in 1995.
